이번 **[꼰대 의사의 정신과 얘기]**에서는
조현병이란 어떤 질환인지,
정신의학에서 말하는 병식은 무엇인지,
조현병 환자가 자신의 증상을 인식하기 어려운 이유,

그리고 환자와 가족이 질환을 함께 이해하고 대처하는 방법까지 자세히 알아봅니다.

특히 “본인이 아프다는 사실을 인정하지 않는다면 어떻게 해야 할까요?”, “조현병은 평생 치료해야 하나요?”, “증상이 좋아진 뒤에도 약을 복용해야 할까요?” 등 환자와 보호자들이 궁금해하는 질문들을 함께 살펴봅니다.

조현병은 개인에 따라 증상과 경과가 다양하며, 병식이 부족하다고 해서 치료나 회복이 불가능한 것은 아닙니다. 적절한 치료와 지속적인 관리, 주변의 이해와 지지가 중요합니다.

nuevos.titulo_original: Friends, fight or flight is only one type of stress response.
nuevos.descripcion:
Friends, fight or flight is only one type of stress response.

In 2000, Dr. Shelley Taylor and her team at UCLA described another pattern, which they called "tend and befriend." 

They originally proposed it to explain how females respond to stress, arguing that the classic fight-or-flight model had been built mostly on males.

Tending means protecting yourselt and your young, and befriending means building the social network that helps you do it. Later research has found that men show these responses too.
I gravitate towards "tend and befriend" myself.

When I feel overstimulated or something goes wrong, I pick up the phone and ask someone how I can help.

Regardless of which you lean towards, fear is only the first response. Being courageous is a choice, and it is trainable.

nuevos.descripcion:
A new, larger randomized trial just put vitamin K2 back in the spotlight for arterial calcification.

Vitamin K2 activates Matrix Gla Protein (MGP), which helps inhibit the formation and growth of calcium crystals within the arterial wall. That makes it biologically plausible that vitamin K2 could slow coronary artery calcification.

And in this new 2-year randomized trial, vitamin K2 MK-7 did exactly that: people supplementing with vitamin K2 experienced less progression of coronary artery calcification than those receiving placebo.

That sounds great—but there’s an important catch.

More coronary artery calcium is associated with greater cardiovascular disease risk, but calcified plaque itself is generally considered more stable than softer forms of plaque.

So simply reducing calcification doesn’t automatically mean you’re reducing cardiovascular risk.

The study did NOT measure soft plaque. This leaves open an important question: did vitamin K2 reduce the overall progression of atherosclerosis, or did it simply alter how much of the plaque became calcified?

It also wasn’t designed to determine whether vitamin K2 reduces heart attacks or other cardiovascular events.
